summary: Session lease extension causes unexpected rollout diversion during canary cutover
description:
Issue summary: Customer StreamlineAI reports that during a scheduled canary cutover for redwood-7b-v2 -> redwood-7b-v2-quant, a subset of sessions remained bound to the old model because their session leases were extended by edge clients. This prevented expected canary traffic split and led to traffic diversion to fallback routes which do not respect the rollout weight.

Impact: ~12% of requests for the customer were routed to fallback model variants for a 30-minute window during the cutover, causing degraded output quality and higher token cost. No user-data leak observed. Customer experienced elevated error counts and asked for rollback.

Environment: production, dedicated pool in us-east-1. Affected tenant: streamlineai-prod, model family redwood-7b-v2.

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Initiate canary cutover in Console with 10% weight to new variant.
2) Multiple long-lived chat sessions with streaming SSE clients maintain active prefix caches and request lease extension calls every 5 minutes.
3) During node drain and promote, session-manager honors existing leases longer than expected (observed up to 45 minutes).
4) Requests tied to those sessions bypass canary routing decision since routing uses session-lease affinity table with TTL > rollout commit time.
5) Requests fall back to pre-configured fallback policy when the primary cohort is unavailable, which reverted them to older quantized variant.

Observed logs and metrics:
- edge-proxy logs show session-lease-extend calls from customer IP ranges at 03:14:22Z.
- routing-service trace: decision=AFFINITY_ENFORCED lease_ttl=2700s session_id=abc123
- console rollout events show canary-weight-commit at 03:10:05Z, promote-window=30m.
- spike in token-cost metric for tenant at 03:20–03:50Z.

Customer asks: revert to original behavior (respect short lease TTL during rollout) or provide guidance to avoid diversion on next cutover.
steps_to_reproduce: Start canary with 10% weight to new model
Create long-lived SSE streaming sessions that call lease-extend
Trigger node drain/promote on serving pool
Observe affinity table entries persisting past rollout commit and requests routing to fallback
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Initial report received from customer; they saw content regression and asked for immediate rollback. Shared request id and sample sessions.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Evan Chen: Acknowledged. Reproduced routing behavior in staging cluster with synthetic SSE clients. Opening investigation. Link to reproduce script: https://bit.ly/replicate-lease-issue
2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE-OnCall (Marcus Lee): Observed extended lease TTLs in session-manager metrics during drain. Suspect lease extension handler does not consult rollout-in-progress flag.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Product (Sofia Ramirez): Customer asks for short-term mitigation: an admin option to enforce session-lease-truncate during rollout. Filing product request for Console toggle.
2026-03-11 13:10 - Evan Chen: Added temporary routing override to honor rollout commit for affected tenant; routing logs show immediate rebalancing. Monitoring for side effects.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: session-manager honors client-requested lease extensions unconditionally; routing uses session affinity table which takes precedence over new rollout weights.
Checked codepath: session-manager/lease_handler does not check rollout_state; missing check added to backlog.
Staging reproduce script shows that when lease TTL > rollout_grace_period, routing will preserve affinity to pre-cutover cohort.
Observed that fallback routes are selected when primary host pool is under drain; because session affinity pointed to draining host group, requests hit fallback policy.
mitigation_actions: Applied tenant-scoped routing override to temporarily ignore session affinity for streamlineai-prod during active rollout (manual intervention) on 2026-03-11 12:52.
Advised customer to avoid client lease-extend calls during cutover as short-term mitigation.
Raised console feature request for 'truncate-session-leases-during-rollout' toggle (tracked in product backlog).
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-scoped routing override removed session-affinity enforcement and traffic rebalanced to canary at 12:52 UTC 2026-03-11. No further regressions observed after rebalancing.

Planned fix: Add rollout-aware lease handling in session-manager to honor a max_rollout_ttl when a rollout is in progress. Patch scheduled: routing#2314 targets hotfix to check rollout_state before honoring lease-extension. ETA for rollout-aware fix to staging: 2026-03-18.

Follow-up: product will add Console toggle to enforce lease truncation during rollout; owner Sofia Ramirez. Customer follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-13 to confirm acceptability of mitigation and rollout plan.
postmortem_followup: Create unit/integration tests for lease-handling during rollouts
Audit other affinity sources (edge cookies, jwt tokens) for similar behavior
Add observability: alert when >5% of tenant requests use fallback route during rollout window
